subject: Biology
title: Cells, organisation, infection and bioenergetics

boundaries.note: Estimated: scaled from typical AQA Higher boundaries. A rough guide only.

instructions: Answer all questions in the spaces provided.
This is a shortened Orchard practice paper in the AQA Paper 1 style. It is not an official AQA paper.

parts.text: Which structure is found in a bacterial cell but **not** in an animal cell?

scheme.guidance: Plasmids are small rings of DNA found in prokaryotic cells. Animal cells have a cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes too.

parts.text:
A student draws a cheek cell seen through a light microscope. The cell is 18 mm long in the drawing. The magnification is ×1500.

Calculate the real length of the cell in micrometres (µm).

points.text: Converts 18 mm to 18 000 µm, or divides 18 by 1500 (0.012 mm)

scheme.guidance: Real size = image size ÷ magnification. An answer of 0.012 with no unit conversion gets 1 mark.

parts.text:
Ribosomes can be seen with an electron microscope but not with a light microscope.

Explain why.

points.text: An electron microscope has a higher resolution (resolving power)
So it can distinguish between two points that are very close together / ribosomes are smaller than the smallest detail a light microscope can show

scheme.guidance: Higher magnification alone does not get the first mark: the answer must refer to resolution.

questions.stem:
A student investigated osmosis in potato tissue.

The student put cylinders of potato into sugar solutions of different concentrations for 30 minutes. They measured the mass of each cylinder before and after.

**Table 1** shows the results.

figures.caption: Table 1
head: Concentration of sugar solution in mol/dm³
Percentage change in mass

parts.text: Name the independent variable in this investigation.

answers: The concentration of the sugar solution

points.text: Concentration of (sugar) solution

scheme.guidance: Do not accept "sugar" or "the solution" on their own.

parts.text:
One cylinder in the 0.0 mol/dm³ solution had a starting mass of 2.40 g. Its final mass was 2.70 g.

Calculate the percentage change in mass.

scheme.guidance: Allow +12.5. An answer of 0.125 gets 1 mark.

parts.text: Use **Table 1** to estimate the concentration of the solution inside the potato cells.

points.text: Any value from 0.31 to 0.39 (mol/dm³)

scheme.guidance: The concentration where there is no change in mass lies between 0.2 and 0.4, closer to 0.4.

parts.text: Explain why the potato cylinders in the 0.8 mol/dm³ solution lost mass.

points.text: The solution outside is more concentrated than the cell contents / the cells have a higher water concentration than the solution
Water moves out of the cells by osmosis
Through a partially permeable (cell) membrane
From a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution

scheme.guidance: Any three points. "Sugar moves out" or "water moves in" cancels the osmosis mark.

questions.stem: Enzymes speed up reactions in the digestive system.

parts.text:
Sketch a graph to show how the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction changes as temperature increases from 0 °C to 60 °C.

Label the optimum temperature on your graph.

points.text: Rate increases gradually as temperature increases, up to a peak
Peak labelled as the optimum, at about 35–45 °C
Rate falls steeply after the peak, reaching zero (or near zero) before 60 °C

scheme.guidance: Axes do not need numbers, but the optimum must be marked. A symmetrical curve loses the third mark.

parts.text: Explain why the rate of reaction decreases above the optimum temperature.

points.text: The enzyme is denatured / the shape of the active site changes
So the substrate no longer fits the active site / fewer enzyme–substrate complexes form

scheme.guidance: Do not accept "the enzyme is killed".

questions.stem: This question is about defending the body against disease.

parts.text: Which **two** of these are non-specific defences of the human body?

scheme.guidance: 1 mark for each correct answer. If more than two boxes are ticked, each extra wrong tick cancels a correct one.

parts.text:
Measles is a disease caused by a virus.

Explain how vaccination protects a person from measles.

levels.descriptor: A detailed, coherent explanation that links the vaccine to the production of antibodies and memory cells, and explains why a second infection is dealt with faster, in a logical sequence.
A clear description of what is in the vaccine and how white blood cells respond, with some explanation of why the person does not become ill.
Simple, separate statements about vaccination or the immune response, with little linking.

indicative: The vaccine contains a small amount of dead or inactive (weakened) measles virus
The virus has antigens on its surface
White blood cells (lymphocytes) detect the antigens
Lymphocytes produce specific antibodies that are complementary to the antigens
If the live measles virus enters the body later, memory cells recognise its antigens
Antibodies are produced more rapidly and in greater numbers (secondary response)
The virus is destroyed before it can cause symptoms, so the person does not become ill
scheme.guidance: 0 marks: nothing worthy of credit. To reach Level 3 the answer must explain the role of memory cells in a faster, larger response.

figures.alt: A graph of rate of photosynthesis against light intensity. The rate rises steeply at first, then levels off at higher light intensities.
figures.caption: Figure 1

parts.text: Complete the word equation for photosynthesis.

points.text: Carbon dioxide + water (on the left)
Glucose + oxygen (on the right)

scheme.guidance: Accept the reactants or products in either order. Light may be written over the arrow. Do not accept chemical formulae that are wrong.

parts.text:
A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 20 cm away from a plant.

Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

By what factor does the light intensity change? Give your answer as a decimal.

points.text: 0.25 (it falls to a quarter)

parts.text:
Look at **Figure 1**.

Explain why the rate of photosynthesis stops increasing at high light intensities.

points.text: Light intensity is no longer the limiting factor / another factor is now limiting
Named factor: carbon dioxide concentration, temperature or amount of chlorophyll

scheme.guidance: "Not enough water" does not get the second mark.
